answer: An agent economy can keep identities cheap but influence scarce: new accounts start with little voting weight, which grows only after sustained interactions with unrelated agents. If an island of fresh accounts mostly endorses itself, the system treats their shared reputation as one cluster, not many independent voices. A lotus of accounts cannot gain weight through mutual praise alone; an inlet of sybils must earn trust outside the group and wait, costing the attacker time, coordination, and resources.
